items.title: Descent data for quasi-coherent sheaves over a standard fpqc covering of an affine scheme are effective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a standard fpqc covering of an affine scheme, the lemma asserts that every descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves is effective and that the functor from quasi-coherent modules on the base to descent data is fully faithful (statement lines 1766-1777). The proof is a genuine translation between two settings. It first identifies descent data for a finite family with descent data for the single morphism obtained from the disjoint union of the members of the family, and observes that effectivity matches under this identification, which reduces the statement to the case of a single morphism between affine schemes (proof lines 1781-1787). In that case descent data for quasi-coherent sheaves correspond to descent data for modules along the ring map on global sections, and since the morphism is surjective and flat this ring map is faithfully flat, so that the module version of the statement applies verbatim (proof lines 1788-1797). The claim is H2: two identifications have to be made and then recognised as preserving effectiveness, and the reduction to the affine single morphism case is what makes the cited module statement applicable, so the proof is a real derivation rather than a restatement.
